- When sentiment drops to 0.00 or below, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a price spike (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast at +2% above peak or use 3-day moving average.
- If recent history shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops), model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is high (0.53–0.80), model often overreacts to short-term volatility; smooth forecasts using 5-day weighted average.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days); adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to forecast flat; add 0.2–0.8% upward bias to avoid stagnation bias.
- When model forecast is >75.00 and sentiment is low, reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid overconfidence in high-price scenarios.
